headline: The grader learned the clap-test page, and the page learned the human thumb
lede: Jon's phone recordings of /claptest were posting false FAILs (the evidence grader had no driver for the calibration page) and his slaps were vanishing before the pad stream (an isPrimary filter dropped every secondary pointer — the slapping hand, whenever a thumb grips the phone). Both fixed with receipts: three stored takes now replay bit-exact, three full Gauntlet sessions close the big build's replay acceptance lines, and a two-finger CDP pin keeps the thumb case honest.

notes.text: #2514 merged: plaicraft:evidence gained the claptest replay driver — Jon's three phone takes (seed144524/828591/978353) replay-verify 3/3 bit-exact, voice 3/3 clock-sane, corrected PASS verdicts posted on #1711; offline self-test 48/48 with a dropped-slap mutant naming its tick.

#2518: the slap target stopped dropping second-finger pointers. The audio audit (#2504) found the real blocker on Jon's phone: loud full-scale claps in audio, zero A-taps in pads — a thumb on the glass makes every slap a secondary pointer, silently discarded. New CDP two-finger pin (thumb held, slaps with other ids) goes RED with the old filter restored.

Acceptance lines #1+#2 of the PLAICRAFT big build now carry receipts: gauntlet seed10 (valkyrie), seed76 (warrior), seed12 (wizard) — three jalfern sessions in the store, replay-verified 100% with native human seats. JON_KEY landed as an Actions secret (#2487 answered): the nightly grades takes autonomously, so a completed human clap test self-verifies ±50 ms.

Lesson: a take-carrying page needs its replay-driver branch the day it records — every /claptest take stored before #2514 became a false FAIL the moment the nightly was armed. And Chromium's first multi-point touch event behaves differently from later ones: warm it up before counting.
